status: evidence-informed candidate seed; research reviewed for scientific accuracy; requires safe merge with existing exercise library and current app schema
uiPrinciples: Keep user-facing category and exercise names familiar and short
Do not show internal evidence tiers, EMG detail, anatomical jargon, or numeric evidence scores on exercise cards
Nerd Facts should normally be 1–2 plain-language sentences
Keep genuine sources attached to Nerd Facts where supported
FOR YOU affects contextual ranking, never exercise eligibility
Do not claim a universal #1 exercise when direct comparative evidence is limited

pectoralis_major_sternocostal.role: Main chest pressing and fly target
notes: Treat the pectoralis major as one large muscle with overlapping regional contributions, not as isolated chunks.
Do not create a separate lower-chest category unless it already exists in the app taxonomy and product rationale supports it.
Incline pressing can shift regional demand toward the clavicular region, but does not isolate it.
Evidence on the exact best angle is mixed and much evidence is acute EMG rather than longitudinal hypertrophy.
Do not count all chest-press sets as complete direct triceps sets without a separate volume model.

anterior_deltoid.role: Secondary contributor especially in higher inclines
notes: Steeper bench inclines often increase anterior-deltoid involvement in acute activation studies.

pectoralis_minor.role: Not a primary exercise-builder target in this pack
notes: Do not label common chest presses as direct pectoralis-minor hypertrophy movements based on the evidence reviewed.

sources.title: Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
supports: progressive resistance training robustly improves muscle size and strength
higher weekly volume tends to support hypertrophy; no single equipment type or many other programming variables consistently dominates
exercise choice should be integrated with an achievable, progressive program
limitations: not a chest-exercise head-to-head review
source search was current to October 2024 even though the review was published in 2026

sources.title: Effects of Horizontal and Incline Bench Press on Neuromuscular Adaptations in Untrained Young Men
sources.sample_summary: 47 untrained young men; three groups trained horizontal, incline, or combined bench press once weekly
supports: all approaches improved strength
one measured pectoralis thickness site changed more in the incline-only group than in the other groups
flat and incline pressing can both be useful; exercise choice can affect regional outcomes
limitations: untrained male sample
once-weekly training protocol
regional site result does not prove incline is universally superior for total chest growth
modest study size and limited number of measured sites

sources.title: Effect of Five Bench Inclinations on the Electromyographic Activity of the Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoid, and Triceps Brachii during the Bench Press Exercise
sources.sample_summary: 30 trained adults tested at 0, 15, 30, 45, and 60 degrees
supports: 30-degree incline produced the highest upper-portion pectoralis EMG among the tested angles in this study
flat bench showed higher middle/lower pectoralis EMG than the steeper angles
anterior-deltoid activity rose at steeper inclines, especially above 45 degrees
limitations: acute EMG is not long-term hypertrophy evidence
other studies show partly inconsistent regional EMG patterns
angle, technique, equipment and participant characteristics affect results

sources.title: Influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation during bench press exercise
sources.sample_summary: 14 resistance-trained men; flat, 30-degree, 45-degree and decline bench presses
supports: incline angles changed some activation patterns during parts of the lift
whole-concentric upper-pectoral EMG was not different across all angles
flat pressing remained a reasonable broad pectoralis option
limitations: acute EMG only
some differences occurred only at particular portions of the concentric phase
not a longitudinal hypertrophy comparison

sources.title: Non-uniform excitation of the pectoralis major muscle during flat and inclined bench press exercises
sources.sample_summary: 8 participants; multiple recording sites across the pectoralis major during flat and 45-degree bench press
supports: regional excitation patterns shifted toward clavicular-region sites during incline compared with flat pressing
supports presenting incline as a possible upper-chest emphasis, not a separate-muscle isolation exercise
limitations: very small sample
acute activation, not longitudinal muscle growth
findings may not generalize to all techniques or inclinations

sources.title: Non-uniform excitation of pectoralis major induced by changes in bench press inclination leads to uneven variations in the cross-sectional area measured by panoramic ultrasonography
sources.type: acute exercise study combining EMG and ultrasound
sources.sample_summary: 13 men performed flat and 45-degree incline bench press sessions
supports: flat and incline sessions showed different immediate regional responses in measured pectoralis heads
regional emphasis is plausible and worth considering when choosing a balanced exercise menu
limitations: post-exercise acute changes are not proof of chronic hypertrophy
small sample
do not interpret temporary architecture/CSA changes as permanent muscle growth

sources.title: A systematic review of surface electromyography analyses of the bench press movement task
sources.type: systematic review of acute EMG studies
supports: pectoralis major and triceps are both substantially involved during bench pressing
bench press technique and testing conditions affect activation patterns
limitations: review concerns acute EMG, not exercise-specific long-term growth superiority
EMG amplitude cannot alone rank hypertrophy outcomes

sources.title: Effect of free-weight vs. machine-based strength training on maximal strength, hypertrophy and jump performance: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.sample_summary: 13 studies; 1,016 participants overall; only five studies reported hypertrophy
supports: no significant overall hypertrophy difference detected between free-weight and machine-based training
equipment can be selected for preference, comfort, skill, availability, and progression
limitations: relatively few studies measured hypertrophy
not specific only to chest exercises
lack of detected difference is not proof every machine and free-weight movement is interchangeable

sources.title: Low-load bench press and push-up induce similar muscle hypertrophy and strength gain
sources.sample_summary: 18 young men; nine in each group; low-load bench press versus load-matched push-up variation, twice weekly
supports: both progressive low-load bench press and appropriately scaled push-ups increased pectoralis thickness
bodyweight push-ups can be a useful chest option when difficulty is suitable
limitations: small sample
young men only
specific low-load matching protocol
does not establish that every push-up variant matches every bench press program

sources.title: Effect of Progressive Calisthenic Push-up Training on Muscle Strength and Thickness
sources.sample_summary: 23 moderately trained men; progressive push-ups compared with bench press; training three times weekly
supports: progressive push-up variations can improve upper-body strength
calisthenic progressions are a valid alternative when load/difficulty progresses
limitations: short intervention
small sample
no significant within-group muscle-thickness differences were detected

sources.title: Does Varying Resistance Exercises Promote Superior Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains? A Systematic Review
sources.sample_summary: 8 studies; 241 participants; included studies were young men
supports: systematic exercise variation may affect regional adaptations
exercise variation should be purposeful rather than random or excessively frequent
limitations: small evidence base
included samples were all young men
not chest-specific

sources.title: Resistance training prescription for muscle strength and hypertrophy in healthy adults: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis
sources.type: systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis
sources.sample_summary: 119 studies and 3,364 participants in the hypertrophy network
supports: many reasonable resistance-training prescriptions can produce hypertrophy
multiple-set programs rank well for hypertrophy; exercise choice exists within a broader progressive program
limitations: not chest-exercise-specific
rankings are aggregate across studies and not a universal recipe for every person

sources.title: Machines and free weight exercises: a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing changes in muscle size, strength, and power
sources.sample_summary: Meta-analysis comparing adaptations from machines and free weights
supports: no overall difference in muscle hypertrophy was detected between free weights and machines in included studies
strength gains are partly specific to the modality practiced
limitations: limited number of hypertrophy studies
not chest-specific

sources.title: Specific prime movers' excitation during free-weight bench press variations and chest press machine in competitive bodybuilders
sources.sample_summary: 10 competitive bodybuilders; flat, incline, decline bench and chest-press machine
supports: bench angle and tool changed regional pectoral, triceps, and deltoid activation patterns
machine and free-weight options have different feel/stability and activation profiles
limitations: small sample
acute EMG only
does not establish which exercise produces greater long-term hypertrophy

sources.title: Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Pectoral Muscles
sources.sample_summary: Clinical anatomy review of pectoral muscles
supports: pectoralis major has clavicular and sternocostal/costal regions with overlapping functions
shoulder angle and movement direction relate to which regions contribute
limitations: anatomical reference, not exercise-comparison or hypertrophy trial

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.finding: Strong foundational press with substantial chest and triceps involvement; useful for standardized progressive overload.
nerdFact: The bench press trains your chest along with your triceps and front shoulders. Consistent technique makes it easier to track progress.
limitations: The bench press is not chest-isolation; triceps and anterior deltoids contribute.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.finding: Strong press option with independent dumbbell paths and readily adjustable loading.
nerdFact: Dumbbells let each arm move independently, which may make it easier to find a comfortable pressing path. They still train the chest, triceps and front shoulders together.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Press
exercises.finding: Stable guided-path press that can suit users who prefer less bar-path stabilization.
nerdFact: The Smith machine guides the bar along a fixed path. That can make the movement easier to repeat and progress for some lifters.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Chest Press Machine
exercises.finding: High-practicality chest press; machine versus free-weight choice can be based on comfort, fit, access and progression rather than presumed universal hypertrophy superiority.
nerdFact: A chest-press machine can build chest muscle just like free weights. Pick a machine that fits your body and lets you increase resistance with control.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.finding: A strong upper-chest candidate: incline pressing can shift regional pectoral demand toward the clavicular region, while steeper angles increase shoulder contribution.
nerdFact: A moderate incline changes the pressing angle and can place more emphasis on the upper chest. A very steep incline tends to involve the front shoulders more.
limitations: Regional EMG evidence is not proof that it beats flat pressing for total chest growth.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.finding: Strong upper-chest candidate with independent dumbbell movement; good option when the user can control a repeatable comfortable path.
nerdFact: Incline dumbbell presses train the chest from a different angle than flat presses. Set the bench at a moderate incline so the front shoulders do not take over the movement.
limitations: Evidence supports altered regional emphasis, not complete upper-chest isolation.

exercises.name: Incline Machine Press
exercises.finding: Stable upper-chest press candidate. The particular seat, handle path and angle affect how the exercise feels and where effort is distributed.
nerdFact: The incline machine press gives you an upper-chest pressing option with a guided path. Adjust the seat so the handles line up comfortably with your chest.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Incline Press
exercises.finding: Stable guided incline press option with room for progressive overload.
nerdFact: A Smith-machine incline press combines the inclined pressing angle with a guided bar path. Adjust your setup to find a comfortable shoulder position.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Incline Cable Chest Press
exercises.finding: Cable pressing is a practical alternative when a suitable bench/cable setup permits a stable, comfortable path.
nerdFact: Cables let you adjust the pressing path to your body and setup. The important part is a controlled movement you can progress over time.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Decline Bench Press
exercises.finding: Valid chest pressing variation; it can be offered as an option without claiming that it uniquely isolates the lower chest.
nerdFact: Decline pressing changes the angle of the movement, but it does not isolate a separate lower-chest muscle. Treat it as one useful variation, not a requirement.
limitations: Direct long-term head-to-head hypertrophy evidence for decline versus flat pressing is limited.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Decline Press
exercises.finding: A selectable chest press variation; use when the setup is comfortable and controllable.
nerdFact: Decline dumbbell pressing trains the chest through a declined pressing angle. It is an option, not a movement everyone needs.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Chest Dip
exercises.finding: A compound chest/triceps option when the user has adequate strength and the shoulder position feels comfortable. A forward torso lean often changes the movement toward more chest contribution, but anatomy and technique vary.
nerdFact: Chest dips train both chest and triceps. Use a range that feels controlled and comfortable for your shoulders; dips are optional, not compulsory.
limitations: Direct comparison with other chest exercises for long-term hypertrophy is limited.

exercises.name: Assisted Chest Dip
exercises.finding: Makes the dip pattern more scalable for users who cannot yet perform controlled bodyweight repetitions.
nerdFact: The assistance machine reduces the amount of bodyweight you lift. You can gradually reduce assistance as your strength improves.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.finding: Evidence supports progressive push-up training as a legitimate chest-building option when the variation is challenging and progressed.
nerdFact: Push-ups can build chest muscle. To keep improving, choose a version that is challenging and progress it as you get stronger.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Weighted Push-Up
exercises.finding: Adds a way to progress push-ups when standard repetitions are no longer sufficiently challenging.
nerdFact: Adding a secure load can make push-ups harder as you grow stronger. Use a safe setup and keep the movement controlled.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Incline Push-Up
exercises.finding: Useful easier push-up progression; raise hands on a stable surface and lower the surface as strength improves.
nerdFact: Placing your hands on a stable raised surface makes push-ups easier. Lower the surface gradually as you become stronger.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Decline Push-Up
exercises.finding: Feet-elevated push-ups change the pressing angle; the exact muscle emphasis depends on body position and movement. Do not claim they isolate upper chest.
nerdFact: Raising your feet changes the push-up angle and makes it harder for many people. Use a stable surface and a position you can control.
limitations: Direct evidence comparing upper-chest hypertrophy from push-up angles is limited.

exercises.name: Cable Chest Press
exercises.finding: A practical press option if the cable setup allows a stable stance and repeatable range. No evidence establishes it as universally better than bench pressing.
nerdFact: Cable chest presses let you choose a comfortable arm path. Keep your torso steady and use a range you can repeat consistently.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Chest Press
exercises.finding: Unilateral press provides an alternative arm path and also requires the trunk to resist rotation. It is not proven to grow the chest more than bilateral presses.
nerdFact: Training one arm at a time can help you focus on a comfortable pressing path. Keep your torso from twisting as you press.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Cable Fly
exercises.finding: Direct chest accessory with adjustable cable position; strong practical fit, but limited direct long-term trials establish superiority over presses or other fly options.
nerdFact: Cable flyes train the chest as your arms move across your body. Set the cables so you can stretch and squeeze comfortably without using momentum.
limitations: Exercise-specific hypertrophy comparisons among fly variations are sparse.

exercises.name: High-to-Low Cable Fly
exercises.finding: Changes the line of pull for variation; do not label as a proven lower-chest isolator.
nerdFact: High-to-low cable flyes change the direction your hands travel. They still train the chest as a whole, and are not proven to isolate one chest region.
limitations: Direct regional hypertrophy evidence is limited.

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
exercises.finding: A reasonable upper-chest accessory based on arm path and practical targeting; direct long-term trials proving regional superiority are limited.
nerdFact: Low-to-high cable flyes move your hands upward across your body. This can be used as an upper-chest-focused variation, but it does not isolate the upper chest.
limitations: Recommendation is based mainly on movement mechanics and practical fit, not direct exercise-specific hypertrophy trials.

exercises.name: Pec Deck Fly
exercises.finding: Stable chest accessory that can be easy to standardize and progressively load; not proven universally superior to cable or dumbbell flyes.
nerdFact: The pec deck lets you train the chest without needing to balance dumbbells. Adjust the seat so the handles or pads line up comfortably with your chest.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Fly
exercises.finding: Chest accessory with a different resistance profile from presses; control the range and avoid forcing a deep shoulder stretch.
nerdFact: Dumbbell flyes train the chest as your arms open and come together. Use a comfortable stretch instead of forcing your shoulders into an extreme position.
limitations: Direct head-to-head hypertrophy evidence versus presses and other fly types is limited.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
exercises.finding: An upper-chest-focused accessory candidate based on bench angle and movement line, without evidence for guaranteed regional isolation.
nerdFact: Incline dumbbell flyes use an inclined bench to change the chest movement angle. Keep the stretch comfortable and use controlled weights.
limitations: Direct regional hypertrophy comparisons are limited.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Fly
exercises.finding: Machine fly variation for users who prefer a stable guided movement; setup and comfort matter.
nerdFact: A chest-fly machine makes it easier to repeat the same path each set. Adjust the machine to fit your shoulder position and range.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Barbell Floor Press
exercises.finding: A valid press variation with a shorter bottom range because the upper arms contact the floor; it can be useful for comfort or strength-specific goals but is not the default for full chest range.
nerdFact: The floor press stops your upper arms at the floor, so it uses a shorter range than a typical bench press. It can be a useful alternative, depending on your goal and comfort.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Squeeze Press
exercises.finding: A variation for preference and variety; extra inward squeezing is not proven to confer greater chest hypertrophy.
nerdFact: The squeeze press asks you to keep the dumbbells pressed toward each other as you press. It is a variation, not a proven shortcut to extra chest growth.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Chest Press
exercises.finding: Home option when a suitable band/anchor allows progressive resistance and a safe setup.
nerdFact: Resistance bands can provide a chest-press option at home. Secure the band safely and use a version that remains challenging as you improve.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Chest Fly
exercises.finding: Accessible chest accessory when equipment is limited; resistance curve and band tension depend on the setup.
nerdFact: A resistance-band fly brings your arms across your body to train the chest. Make sure the band and anchor are secure before you start.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Low-Incline Barbell Press
exercises.finding: Low-to-moderate incline is a useful starting candidate for upper-chest emphasis; no single exact angle is mandatory or universally optimal.
nerdFact: A low incline changes the press slightly toward the upper chest while usually avoiding the front-shoulder emphasis of a very steep angle.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Low-Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.finding: Practical low-incline press variant for upper-chest emphasis. Keep it only as a distinct record if the current app does not already represent it as an adjustable setup option.
nerdFact: A small bench incline can shift some work toward the upper chest. If your bench adjusts, you may not need a separate exercise record for every angle.
limitations: Do not create duplicate records for different bench-angle settings if the current library treats angle as a setup parameter.

exercises.name: Plate-Loaded Chest Press
exercises.finding: Another machine chest-press style. Keep as an alias to an existing machine press if the library does not distinguish the machine type.
nerdFact: Different chest-press machines can follow different paths. Choose one that fits well and lets you train hard with control.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
exercises.finding: Valid compound press, typically more triceps-focused than a moderate-grip chest press. Keep selectable but do not rank as the default chest-specific match for everyone.
nerdFact: A closer grip usually makes the triceps work harder relative to a wider or moderate grip. It still trains the chest, but it is often chosen for triceps and pressing strength.
limitations: Exercise-specific long-term hypertrophy superiority over other valid options has not been established.

rankingGuardrails: Chest is the broad target; Upper Chest is a regional emphasis, not a separate isolated muscle.
Use the existing visible category identifiers exactly; do not invent near-duplicate taxonomy IDs.
Primary pressing candidates for Chest include flat barbell/dumbbell presses, compatible chest-press machines, and progressive push-up options.
Upper Chest recommendations should favor suitable moderate-incline presses when the user's goal and equipment fit; retain flat presses and all other valid alternatives as selectable.
Do not make 30 degrees or any exact incline mandatory; 30 degrees showed more upper-portion EMG in one study, while evidence across studies is not fully consistent.
Do not claim EMG proves long-term hypertrophy superiority.
Do not claim cable fly, pec deck, or dumbbell fly is universally superior to presses; treat flyes as useful complementary options where equipment and user preference fit.
Do not claim free weights are universally better than machines for hypertrophy; current meta-analysis did not detect an overall hypertrophy difference.
Push-ups are valid chest options when suitably challenging and progressively scaled; do not suppress them because they are bodyweight.
Goal and physique priority can modify contextual scores and FOR YOU qualification but never act as hard exercise filters.
Map internal targets to existing library records by stable ID and normalized name/aliases; update matches rather than duplicate.
Some exercise rows are candidate aliases or angle variants. If the app represents bench angle as a setup parameter, merge these aliases into the existing exercise rather than create duplicates.
Every equipment requirement must reflect real equipment; do not bring back the previously fixed equipment over-filter bug.
A FOR YOU badge should come from the shared existing recommendation logic; do not hard-code the badge to an exercise name.
